routing.reason: Input validation and error handling in one small API (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts), one client handler (public/app.js) and tests, with fully specified acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: workflow default, not hotfix — a validation bug with explicit criteria, no outage, so the plan gate and full review stay — cost if wrong: a slightly slower delivery.

Ruling: PRD, architecture, UX and SEO skipped — the criteria are explicit, the design is one validation helper, and the only UI change is showing an existing error message in an existing #error element — cost if wrong: a missed design question, cheap to fix.
Ruling: frame kept at low effort — it checks the edge cases the ticket leaves open — cost if wrong: a few cents spent on a ticket that was already clear.

Ruling: security review at medium — the diff parses untrusted request bodies and changes what error text leaves the server (criterion 5), but touches no authentication, payments or dependencies — cost if wrong: a missed leak of an internal message.

Ruling: a JSON body that is valid but not an object (null, an array, a number) answers 400 {"error": "invalid JSON body"} — today body.title throws a TypeError and answers 500, which criterion 5 and the intent of criterion 4 forbid — cost if wrong: a one-line change in the validator.

Ruling: PATCH validates the title only when the key `title` is present in the body (`title: null` or `""` is rejected with 400 "title is required"); a PATCH without `title` keeps working — matches criterion 2 — cost if wrong: a PATCH {done:true} regression, which a test covers.
Ruling: the server logs the real error with console.error and sends only {"error": "internal error"} — criterion 5 — cost if wrong: a leak of internal detail, which the security review checks.

Ruling: the 200-character limit counts characters of the trimmed title, and the saved title is trimmed on both POST and PATCH — criterion 3 — cost if wrong: a boundary off-by-one, which tests at 200 and 201 cover.
Ruling: the page fix goes in the submit handler of public/app.js: catch the failed POST and call the existing show(err) — criterion 6 — cost if wrong: the empty-task click would still look dead.
Ruling: no squad, since the project declares none; the lead plans the whole ticket as one batch with back and front tasks, tests written by the back developer — cost if wrong: none.

first: test/tasks.test.ts(143,95): error TS7006: Parameter 't' implicitly has an 'any' type.

criteria.why: createTask calls validateTitle, which throws 400 'title is required' for missing, empty, blank or non-string titles before any insert; tests cover these.
updateTask validates when 'title' is in changes, and app.ts only passes title when the key is present; validation runs before the update, and tests cover it.
validateTitle trims, rejects more than 200 characters with the exact message, and returns the trimmed value, which is saved; tests check the 200/201 boundary and trimming.
readJson turns a JSON.parse failure into HttpError 400 'invalid JSON body'. It does the same for non-object JSON, which goes slightly beyond the ticket but is reasonable.
The catch handler logs with console.error and sends a generic 'internal error'. It handles headersSent, and a test checks that nothing leaks and the error is logged.
The submit handler catches errors from api() and calls show(err). This assumes api() throws with the API's error message, which the diff doesn't show.
New tests cover POST, PATCH, length, invalid JSON and the 500 case. The page change is untested, which is acceptable.

findings.what: PATCH checks `"title" in body`, so `{"title": undefined}` can't occur in JSON, but PATCH with `done` of a non-boolean type is still unvalidated. This is out of scope for the ticket but still a latent hole.
Non-object JSON bodies (null, arrays, numbers) now return 400 'invalid JSON body'. This is beyond the literal ticket, though it prevents a 500 on `"title" in null`.
The PATCH line builds two different objects to work around the `in` check, and the long ternary line is awkward. Passing `body` fields conditionally would be cleaner.
Mocking DatabaseSync.prototype.prepare with t.mock depends on the implementation, and the front-end change (item 6) has no test.
readJson still has no body size limit, and a malformed request stream error would be a 500. Neither is in scope.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion with a small HttpError and validateTitle design. It sends a safe generic 500 and logs the real error on the server. The tests are thorough on boundaries and on the PATCH-unchanged case; the only gaps are minor ones, such as no test for the front-end change and a slightly awkward PATCH line.
